TEAMS.name: Bone Clan
TEAMS.doctrine: Attrition through mass conscription; feed the front with anyone who can be chained up and pointed forward.
TEAMS.army: Thousands of conscripted mobs and crawlers, ranked by carved bone tokens nobody outranks the warlord for holding.
reputation: Won last season by simply outlasting everyone else.
Feared less for skill than for how little the warlord seems to care who dies.

TEAMS.name: The Reavers
TEAMS.doctrine: Hit fast, take the supply lines first, worry about the throne room later.
TEAMS.army: Light raiders on stolen vehicles; long on speed, short on anything that can absorb a real siege.
reputation: Will break a truce the instant it stops being useful.

TEAMS.name: Prism Kingdom
TEAMS.doctrine: Fortify, refract, outlast. Every wall is angled to bounce something back at whoever's shooting.
TEAMS.army: Glass-armored knights and light-bending spellslingers; slow to mobilize, brutal to besiege.
reputation: Hasn't lost a defended position in two seasons.
Never confirms a warlord until the ceasefire ends.
TEAMS.canon_note: the Kingdom never confirms a warlord until the ceasefire ends

TEAMS.name: Blood Sultanate
TEAMS.doctrine: Overwhelming force at a single point, chosen by the warlord personally and never explained in advance.
TEAMS.army: Desert-drilled heavy infantry backed by a cavalry wing the Sultanate insures at absurd cost.
reputation: Eliminated first two seasons ago in a single afternoon.
Sponsor pulled funding mid-season once already.

TEAMS.name: The Madness
TEAMS.sponsor: no sponsor — the Syndicate can't get anyone at the door to answer the phone
TEAMS.doctrine: None that survives contact with the next warlord. Strategy changes by the hour.
TEAMS.army: Whoever wandered in and didn't leave; morale is either unbreakable or nonexistent, never in between.
reputation: Nobody can predict them, including their own officers.
Somehow still fielding an army after three seasons of losses.

TEAMS.name: Operatic Collective
TEAMS.doctrine: Every battle is a performance; the Collective would rather lose beautifully than win quietly.
TEAMS.army: Armored chorus lines with genuine magical resonance behind the theatrics — the sound is the weapon.
reputation: Highest audience ratings of any team, win or lose.
Warlord has never once broken character on camera.

TEAMS.name: Lemig Sortion
TEAMS.sponsor: House Sortion's own treasury — no outside sponsor needed
TEAMS.doctrine: Old money, older grudges. Buy what can be bought; the rest gets besieged at leisure.
TEAMS.army: A small, extremely well-equipped household guard, backed by mercenary contracts it can renew indefinitely.
reputation: Has personally funded at least one rival's collapse in the past.
Warlord is also the sponsor, which everyone pretends not to notice.

TEAMS.name: The Dream
TEAMS.sponsor: unknown; nobody's cashed a check from them, but everyone's afraid to ask
TEAMS.doctrine: Unclear. Territory it takes tends to stay eerily quiet afterward.
TEAMS.army: Numbers nobody agrees on. Scouts report different totals every time.
reputation: Some crawlers swear the same soldier has died in three different battles.
The Syndicate's cameras have unexplained gaps whenever it fights.

TEAMS.name: The Scrapheap Banner
TEAMS.sponsor: whatever the crawler collective could scrape together this week
TEAMS.doctrine: Take the ground nobody else wants yet, dig in, and make being ignored expensive.
TEAMS.army: A scrappy mutual-defense pact of crawlers, conscripts, and defectors who'd rather not die for someone else's banner.
reputation: Formed during this season's ceasefire; no history yet.
The one team actively recruiting crawlers instead of just conscripting them.

FORTRESS: A repurposed stadium with the seats torn out for barracks.
A cathedral converted into a war room; the pews are gone and the altar is a map table.
A flooded parking structure turned moat-fortress, three levels underwater on purpose.
A skyscraper with every window bricked over and murder holes cut in instead.
A rail yard fortified with shipping containers stacked four high.
An old amusement park; the rides still run, mostly as early-warning noise.
A grain silo complex, tunneled through and wired with alarms.
A collapsed overpass turned into a stronghold, traffic-cone orange and paranoid.
A university campus walled in with its own library shelving.
A power plant, its cooling towers repurposed as watchtowers.
WILDCARD_SPONSOR: No sponsor; the crowdfund is the sponsor now.
A dropped sponsor picked back up out of pity.
Whoever's ad ran during the recruitment stream.
A rival team's leftover budget, laundered through a shell contract.
WILDCARD_DOCTRINE: Whatever works today; there is no five-year plan.
Grab territory nobody else wants yet and dig in.
Recruit anyone who can hold a weapon and doesn't ask about the contract.
Win ugly, win late, apologize never.

ceasefire: {A} and {B} trade border surveys and pretend not to be scouting each other's walls.
{A} quietly offers {B} a non-aggression pact neither intends to honor.
A joint scrimmage between {A} and {B} runs long enough that the Syndicate cuts the feed.
{A}'s sponsor leaks {B}'s roster to the betting boards early.
{A} spends the ceasefire buying rounds of drinks in {B}'s territory, memorizing exits.
rampup: {A} raids {B}'s supply convoy and returns everything but the food.
{A} and {B} skirmish over a stairwell chamber neither can hold alone.
{A}'s warlord challenges {B}'s to single combat; only one of them shows up.
{A} salts {B}'s water source out of pure spite.
hostilities: {A}'s primary base falls to a joint push by three other teams.
{A} and {B} fight to a standstill outside Larracos's outer wall.
{A} burns its own supply depot rather than let {B} take it.
{B}'s warlord goes missing; {A} claims credit it can't prove.
{A} opens a second front against {B} while publicly denying it.
peeling: {A}'s castle falls to {B} in a fight the Syndicate replays for a week.
{A} and {B} propose a truce that neither's officers agree to honor.
{A} makes a last play for Larracos and burns most of its army doing it.
{B} salvages what's left of {A} and absorbs its survivors.
{A} refuses to yield even after {B} takes its throne room.

STAIR_SPOTS: behind a curtain of dead vines
under three feet of packed ash
beneath a toppled statue of a forgotten ruler
under a stack of unclaimed shields
under a cairn of enemy dog tags
OFFER_TERMS: a standing contract: fight under their banner, keep your loot, no questions about your gear
conscription with benefits: guaranteed rations, a cot, and a body double for the death feed
officer rank on day one, if you can survive the other officers
a mercenary rate paid per confirmed kill, audited by the Syndicate
full amnesty for anything you did on Floor 8, in writing
OFFER_HOOKS: The recruiter hasn't blinked once during this pitch.
Somewhere behind them, someone is quietly disposing of the last recruit's gear.
They already know your name, which nobody told them.
The contract is real. The pen is not.
They're recruiting everyone on this floor. Every single team.
HELP_MISSIONS: Escort a supply run through contested territory.
Clear a stairwell chamber the winner's army hasn't reached yet.
Feed the winner's warlord bad intelligence about a rival, on purpose, in their favor.
Hold a bottleneck long enough for the winner's main force to arrive.
Recover a defector the winner wants back alive.
HINDER_MISSIONS: Sabotage a supply cache before the winner's quartermasters reach it.
Leak the winner's troop movements to anyone who'll pay for them.
Steal back a stairwell key the winner is guarding.
Convince one of the winner's officers that defecting is survivable.
Burn a bridge, literally, before the winner's army crosses it.
NEUTRAL_ADVICE: Stick to the forest band; the mob levels are honest and nobody there is voting.
Let the stairwell chambers come to you instead of hunting for them.
Take a recruitment offer just for the perks and never show up to a single battle.
Camp near Larracos's outer wall; both sides need it standing more than they need you dead.
Sell information to whoever's currently losing; they pay better and ask fewer questions.
OUTCOME_CRITERIA: Killing a warlord early enough resets who's favored to win.
Holding a throne room for the full six hours flips an elimination.
Feeding one team accurate intel about another changes the timeline's raids.
Taking the crawler-friendly team's side (or against it) shifts the blocs.
Every stairwell chamber the party clears is one less bargaining chip for whoever was guarding it.
Surviving to the Peeling with a reputation intact opens better recruitment offers.

RETRIBUTION.name: The Retribution
RETRIBUTION.note: Larracos's standing garrison; NPC regulars with home-field advantage and no sponsor to answer to.
